_comment: Citations for the Transport core rules (10e). Wahapedia source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/the-rules/core-rules/#TRANSPORTS. Disembark and Firing Deck quoted_text re-verified verbatim 2026-07-08 against the live page (the prior transcriptions had drifted from the actual rule text — see simulator.transport_play_disembark_full_acts for what changed).

simulator.embark.quoted_text: If a unit makes a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move, and every model in that unit ends that move within 3" of a friendly TRANSPORT model, they can embark within it. A unit cannot embark if it has already disembarked from a TRANSPORT model in the same phase. Remove the unit from the battlefield and place it to one side - it is now embarked within that TRANSPORT model. Unless otherwise stated, units cannot do anything or be affected in any way while they are embarked.
simulator.embark.trigger: owning player's Movement phase; an eligible unit ends its move with every model within 3" of a friendly TRANSPORT that has remaining capacity
simulator.embark.effect: the unit is removed from the battlefield and tracked as a passenger on the transport. It cannot act normally while embarked. SwegHammer models this with passenger.embarked_in = transport (back-pointer) and transport.passengers append; activation gates in _do_move / _do_shoot / _do_charge / _do_fight return early for any unit with embarked_in set, and ranged targeting filters embarked units out of the candidate list. First-pass: pre-game embark only — the deploy pass embarks one INFANTRY squad per available TRANSPORT (capacity hardcoded to 12 INFANTRY models).

simulator.disembark.quoted_text: If a unit from your army starts your Movement phase embarked within a TRANSPORT model, that unit can disembark in that phase. When a unit disembarks from a TRANSPORT model, set it up on the battlefield so that it is wholly within 3" of that TRANSPORT model and not within Engagement Range of any enemy models. If, for any reason, a disembarking model cannot be set up, that model's unit cannot disembark. Units that disembark from a TRANSPORT model that either Remained Stationary this phase or has not yet made a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move this phase can then act normally (make a Normal move, Advance, shoot, declare a charge, fight, etc.) in the remainder of the turn. Such a disembarking unit cannot choose to Remain Stationary. Units that disembark from a TRANSPORT model that made a Normal move this phase count as having made a Normal move themselves; they cannot move further during this phase. Such a unit also cannot declare a charge in the same turn, but can otherwise act normally in the remainder of the turn. Units cannot disembark from a TRANSPORT model that either Advanced or Fell Back this turn.
simulator.disembark.trigger: owning player's Movement phase; the unit is embarked at the start of the phase and the transport has not Advanced or Fallen Back this turn
simulator.disembark.effect: the passenger is placed wholly within 3" of the transport's position and not within Engagement Range of an enemy. SwegHammer searches a spiral of candidate offsets (cardinals first, then diagonals) up to 3" away; if all are blocked the disembark is skipped (no fallback-through-blocked-terrain path modelled). Voluntary disembark fires in _do_move BEFORE the transport's own move decision for that activation, so it always satisfies the rule's first (full-acts) branch. Which branch actually governs the passenger's rest-of-turn rights is now correctly modelled by simulator.transport_play_disembark_full_acts (see that entry) — this entry covers WHERE and WHEN disembark is offered, not the acts lockout. Heuristic for WHY it disembarks: near an objective (<=6") or the transport is below 50% HP, plus (SWEG_TRANSPORT_PLAY only) a shoot or charge opportunity — see simulator.transport_play_disembark_intelligence. First-pass: skips the >3" emergency-disembark fallback and the 'cannot choose to Remain Stationary' nuance (not modelled — no distinct Remain-Stationary declaration exists in SwegHammer's move model).

simulator.transport_play_disembark_full_.rule_name: Transport (Disembark) — acts-lockout correction, and Destroyed Transport's charge carve-out
simulator.transport_play_disembark_full_.quoted_text: Units that disembark from a TRANSPORT model that either Remained Stationary this phase or has not yet made a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move this phase can then act normally (make a Normal move, Advance, shoot, declare a charge, fight, etc.) in the remainder of the turn. Units that disembark from a TRANSPORT model that made a Normal move this phase count as having made a Normal move themselves; they cannot move further during this phase. Such a unit also cannot declare a charge in the same turn, but can otherwise act normally in the remainder of the turn. [Destroyed Transports, same page:] Until the end of the turn, that unit counts as having made a Normal move this turn, and cannot declare a charge this turn.
simulator.transport_play_disembark_full_.trigger: SWEG_TRANSPORT_PLAY=1 (default OFF); a passenger is disembarked via simulator._disembark, either voluntarily (before its transport's own move — SwegHammer's only voluntary ordering, so always the 'has not yet moved' branch) or forced (transport destroyed, simulator.destroyed_transport — the codex's own carve-out, unaffected by movement timing)
simulator.transport_play_disembark_full_.effect: CORRECTS a long-standing approximation. Before this gate: EVERY disembark (voluntary or forced) blocked the passenger's own further movement this round (_disembarked_this_round read by _do_move) and NEITHER blocked charging — backwards from the real rule on both counts for the two cases SwegHammer actually produces. With the gate ON: a voluntary disembark (always the 'has not yet moved' branch here) does NOT add the passenger to _did_move_this_round / _disembarked_this_round, leaving it free to move further this phase (if its own _do_move activation slot for the round has not already elapsed — see the ordering caveat in _maybe_disembark_before_move's docstring), shoot, and charge, exactly like an on-foot unit. A forced (Destroyed Transport) disembark keeps the movement lockout AND is newly added to _forced_disembark_charge_locked_this_round, read by _do_charge to block its charge this turn — the restriction the codex actually applies to that case, which the pre-gate code was missing entirely. Gate OFF preserves the prior approximation byte-identical.

simulator.transport_play_disembark_intel.rule_name: Transport (Disembark) — piloting heuristic: disembark when the passenger has a job
simulator.transport_play_disembark_intel.quoted_text: Units that disembark from a TRANSPORT model that either Remained Stationary this phase or has not yet made a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move this phase can then act normally (make a Normal move, Advance, shoot, declare a charge, fight, etc.) in the remainder of the turn.
simulator.transport_play_disembark_intel.trigger: SWEG_TRANSPORT_PLAY=1 (default OFF); evaluated in _maybe_disembark_before_move alongside the always-on near-objective/damaged-transport heuristic. BOTH new triggers require firing_deck<=0 (a transport WITH a working Firing Deck keeps its passenger aboard — see effect). SHOOT: a live enemy is within [3" disembark radius + the passenger's own weapon range] of the transport. CHARGE: a live enemy is within [3" disembark radius + the passenger's Move + 12" charge-pick radius, matching pick_charge_target's own threat window] of the transport.
simulator.transport_play_disembark_intel.effect: ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC, not a new codex rule — it decides WHEN the real Disembark rule (simulator.disembark) is worth invoking. Fills the gap named at the wave-246 rejection of squad-level pre-game embark ('whole-squad embark denies first-round shooting... with no disembark-timing intelligence to recover tempo'): a passenger with firing_deck=0 previously only disembarked near an objective or a dying transport, so it could ride the whole game without ever taking a shot even with a live target in range; a passenger could never charge at all while embarked. Both new triggers require firing_deck<=0: a transport WITH a Firing Deck already gives its passenger a guaranteed shot every Shooting phase via the always-on simulator.firing_deck mechanic, and SwegHammer's one-passenger-per-transport pregame embark means once that passenger disembarks the transport's Firing Deck permanently has nobody left to select — an early mechanism check (4 archetype battles, Astra Militarum/Chimera + Orks/Trukk, SWEG_TRANSPORT_PLAY=1) caught the charge trigger evacuating firing-deck transports before they ever fired a shot when it was NOT scoped this way, so the firing_deck<=0 gate was added to both triggers. Both new triggers only ever ADD disembark events (an additional OR condition) and only take effect once simulator.transport_play_disembark_full_acts has restored real charge eligibility to a voluntary disembark — without that fix, adding a charge trigger here would have been pointless (embarked-then-disembarked units could not charge under the pre-fix approximation). Gate OFF: neither trigger is evaluated, byte-identical.

simulator.firing_deck.quoted_text: Some TRANSPORT models have 'Firing Deck x' listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase, you can select up to 'x' models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models' units are not eligible to shoot.
simulator.firing_deck.trigger: the transport is selected to shoot in its Shooting phase and has one or more embarked passenger units that have not already shot this phase
simulator.firing_deck.effect: up to X embarked passenger models also resolve a ranged attack against the same target as the transport, measured from the transport's position. SwegHammer applies this after the transport's own attack lands: it walks the first X passengers (highest Lanchester score by virtue of the embark routine picking best-scorers first), and each that is in range fires one Unit.attack against the target. The codex's 'counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected, in addition to its other weapons' means the shots use the TRANSPORT's own ballistic skill; first-pass uses each passenger's own hit_probability instead because Unit.attack reads BS off the firing profile and there is no BS-override plumbed through it — for Marine transports both are typically 3+ so the divergence is small. The 'units have not already shot this phase' restriction is satisfied for free: an embarked passenger has no activation of its own while embarked, so it cannot have shot before the transport's own Shooting-phase activation calls this method.

simulator.destroyed_transport.quoted_text: If a TRANSPORT model is destroyed, any units embarked within that TRANSPORT model must immediately disembark before that TRANSPORT model is removed from the battlefield. Units that disembark from a destroyed TRANSPORT model are not affected by that model's Deadly Demise ability. Instead, you must roll one D6 for each disembarking model. For each roll of 1, that disembarking model's unit suffers 1 mortal wound. In addition, if a unit disembarks from a destroyed TRANSPORT model: until the start of its controlling player's next Command phase, that unit is Battle-shocked. Until the end of the turn, that unit counts as having made a Normal move this turn, and cannot declare a charge this turn.
simulator.destroyed_transport.trigger: a TRANSPORT's current_health drops to 0 with one or more embarked passengers
simulator.destroyed_transport.effect: every passenger force-disembarks (placed within 3" of the transport's last position via the same spiral search as voluntary disembark), then each model in each disembarking unit rolls 1D6 and is destroyed on a 1. SwegHammer's Unit instance represents a whole squad with pooled current_health, so per-model rolls are computed as models_alive = current_health / (profile.health / profile.min_models); one D6 is rolled per surviving model and current_health is reduced by (kills * wounds_per_model) — an engine-level approximation of the codex's 'suffers 1 mortal wound' per model roll of 1 (mortal wounds are otherwise allocated per the normal damage rules; SwegHammer applies them directly as model kills). DRK-FINAL-2 (2026-05-24) replaced an earlier one-roll-per-Unit implementation that under-modelled losses for multi-model squads. The Battle-shocked status is NOT modelled (no Battle-shock state exists for a forced disembark outside the normal Battle-shock test path — documented gap). The 'counts as having made a Normal move... cannot declare a charge' carve-out IS modelled under SWEG_TRANSPORT_PLAY — see simulator.transport_play_disembark_full_acts. Fires from _maybe_apply_deadly_demise (called at every kill-detection site) before the deadly demise blast, so surviving passengers are correctly placed within demise blast range. Emergency Disembarkation (the >3"-blocked, 6"-radius, 1-3-mortal-wound variant) is NOT modelled — first pass just skips placement if the 3" spiral is fully blocked (documented pre-existing gap, out of scope for this change).

simulator.reembark.rule_name: Embarking (10e Core Rules) — mid-game voluntary re-embark (piloting heuristic)
simulator.reembark.quoted_text: If all models in a unit can be embarked, then the whole of the unit can embark within a friendly TRANSPORT that is within 3" of it. A unit cannot embark and disembark in the same phase (unless otherwise stated).
simulator.reembark.trigger: SWEG_REEMBARK=1 (default OFF, HELD); after a unit finishes its Movement-phase move, it is not embarked, not a TRANSPORT, not within Engagement Range (1") of an enemy, not the sole controller of a nearby objective, and a friendly TRANSPORT with spare capacity is within 3"
simulator.reembark.effect: ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC extending the core embark rule (simulator.embark) to mid-game: the unit re-embarks into the nearest eligible friendly transport via _maybe_reembark_after_move (code/simulator.py, called at the end of _do_move), ending its Shooting/Charge/Fight activations (the existing embarked_in guards enforce that). Fills the documented gap that a disembarked unit was otherwise stuck on foot for the rest of the game. BUILT + HELD default-off (2026-07-01): full-matrix N=40 vs sc29a was NEAR-INERT (very low flip counts, no decisive movers, gated 2.58 -> 2.69 within noise) because the 3" re-embark condition is rarely met in the archetype games; held pending a frame where transports feature more, or a durability-over-reward correction. LEFT ALONE by the 2026-07-08 disembark-timing/firing-deck work (SWEG_TRANSPORT_PLAY) per brief — no interaction: SWEG_REEMBARK gates re-EMBARKING, SWEG_TRANSPORT_PLAY gates disembark-then-act timing and disembark-intelligence triggers; a unit that re-embarks under SWEG_REEMBARK is unaffected by SWEG_TRANSPORT_PLAY until it disembarks again. Off path (SWEG_REEMBARK unset or '0') returns on the first line — byte-identical.
